_comment: Whether a request asks for many files (owner, 2026-10-20), which decides if the per-file batch rule and its examples (`when: many` in prompt.yaml) join its prompt. The clarify gate's own test: a batch word, a plural file word or a glob in the request (its word lists are pinned by nl_clarify_gate_cases.json). What names a place is left out before testing: a URL (its host can read `files.`), and, when the request names a file (a URL names one too), a known folder after in/into/to/on/onto/from, which is then where that file goes (`put clip.mov in my Downloads folder`, `to Documents`); with no file named, the folder may be the batch (`everything in my Videos folder`). A file is named by a name with an extension holding a letter (`clip.mp4`, `x.3gp`); a codec or a number (`H.264`, `1.25`) names none (2026-10-22). A name the request gives an output ("call it preview.gif", "save them as out.mp4", "as audio.mp3", "into c.mp4", "als", "como", "comme", "като", "保存为") is not a file it is about (2026-10-23). A request that names a file is about that file: a batch word alone (`every page of sample.pdf`, `at all`, `every time`) does not make it ask for many; a glob or a plural file word still does. Python `knaif.nl_clarify_gate.asks_for_many_files`, Rust `knaif_core::nl_clarify_gate::asks_for_many_files`.
